notable_claims: Censorship or challenges of textbooks and classic novels were reported at their highest levels in 10 years as of 1992.
The CAF Archive maintained back issues of newsgroup discussions, digests, book reviews, and reports on laws and litigation.
classification.summary: This is a digest abstract summarizing five items related to academic freedom and censorship, including AAUP policy on campus speech codes and reports on textbook censorship. It also provides an update on the CAF Archive's contents and resources for Internet information. The document lists the editorial staff managing the Computers and Academic Freedom news distribution.
classification.title: Abstract of CAF-News 02.44

notable_claims: Rules that ban or punish speech based upon its content cannot be justified in institutions of higher learning.
The distinction between the regulation of the content of speech and the regulation of the manner of speech is untenable in practice.
Free speech is the precondition of the academic enterprise itself.
classification.summary: This item is a policy statement from the American Association of University Professors (AAUP) opposing the implementation of campus speech codes. The AAUP argues that banning speech based on content, including hateful or offensive language, undermines the fundamental academic mission of testing and expanding knowledge. It suggests that institutions should penalize disruptive conduct rather than the content of speech itself.
classification.title: AAUP: On Freedom of Expression and Campus Speech Codes

identity.subject: Article 1--AAUP: "On Freedom of Expression and Campus Speech Codes"

notable_claims: Anti-pornography laws drafted by Dworkin and MacKinnon are argued to have a censoring impact as severe as criminal obscenity laws.
The text claims that anti-censorship feminists believe civil liberties are inextricable from feminist goals.
classification.summary: Joseph F. Mays shares excerpts from the book 'Women Against Censorship' (1985), which features feminist essays opposing anti-pornography legislation. The text discusses the tension between radical feminists who support restrictive laws and those who argue that such measures empower conservative, patriarchal state control over speech. It emphasizes the link between civil liberties and feminist goals.
classification.title: Article 2--Excerpts from women against censorship

notable_claims: Censorship challenges in public schools were at their highest level in 10 years during 1991-92.
376 attacks on the freedom to learn occurred across 44 states.
Religious views were the most frequent rationale for challenging educational materials.
classification.summary: A UPI report details a survey by People for the American Way indicating that book and textbook censorship in public schools reached a ten-year peak during the 1991-92 school year. The report notes that 41% of challenged materials were removed or restricted, often due to religious objections or concerns over profanity and sexuality.
classification.title: Report: Book censorship, challenges in schools at 10-year high

notable_claims: The CAF Archive provided a centralized electronic library for information on computers and academic freedom via FTP and email.
The archive included critiques of private religious university computer policies (e.g., Baylor University).
The archive hosted resources discussing the intersection of anti-harassment laws and university bans on offensive digital material.
classification.summary: This announcement details the structure and contents of the Computers and Academic Freedom (CAF) electronic library hosted by the EFF. It lists available resources including AAUP statements on speech codes, university computer policies, legal documents regarding obscenity and hate crimes, and FAQs on email privacy and Netnews liability.
classification.title: Recent Changes to the CAF Archive

notable_claims: Identifies early key resources for CMC including the WorldWideWeb at info.cern.ch and various anonymous FTP repositories.

classification.summary: A comprehensive directory of Internet and Computer-Mediated Communication (CMC) resources compiled by John December. It provides a curated list of FTP sites, newsgroups, electronic journals, and organizations focused on the technical and social aspects of networking. The document serves as an early map of the digital information landscape during the transition to widespread Internet use.
